<section_guide number="9" title="Out of Scope">
<purpose>Record confirmed product exclusions and known technical debt without inventing a roadmap</purpose>

<questions>
1. What features are explicitly excluded from the MVP? (→ 9.1)
2. What is the confirmed reason for deferring each? Record a target phase only when the user supplied or approved one. (→ 9.1)
3. Is there known technical debt with an observable user or operational consequence? If none is known, record that directly. (→ 9.2)
</questions>

<scope_boundary>
Reuse supplied exclusions and known issues. Do not turn a framework, storage product,
deployment tool, generic testing target, or unresolved product decision into a
deferred Feature. Do not manufacture Phase 2/3 plans to fill a table.
When real items exist, use the tables to record their behavior/consequence, reason,
priority where known, and confirmed phase; use "Not scheduled" if no phase was agreed.
If there are no items, a short "None identified" statement is sufficient.
Section 9 remains a required approval unit; this does not make it optional.
</scope_boundary>

<example>
Example input: the user has identified no deferred product behavior or known technical debt.

### 9.1 Deferred Features

None identified.

### 9.2 Technical Debt Roadmap

No known technical debt.

</example>

<important>Keep 9.1 Deferred Features and 9.2 Technical Debt Roadmap separate. Use tables for supplied items and a direct absence statement when there are none.</important>
<completion>Confirm the actual exclusions and known debt, including an explicit absence when applicable, before saving both required subsections.</completion>
</section_guide>
